Section 01

Program
Design

Section 01 — Program Design · 1 of 10

Volleyball Arm Action

Which exercise is more useful for a volleyball player's arm action?
  • AFront Raise
  • BBicep Curl

Likely answer: A — Front Raise

Why
Volleyball arm action = shoulder flexion (arm swings forward/up).
Front raise trains the same movement → better transfer.
Bicep curl = elbow flexion only → little carryover.
Section 01 — Program Design · 2 of 10

Lineman Push Movement

Which exercise best improves an American football lineman's pushing arm movement?
  • ASupine Bench Press
  • BMed Ball Chest Pass
  • CIncline Dumbbell Press

Likely answer: C — Incline Dumbbell Press

Why
Lineman drives from a forward-leaning trunk → incline angle matches.
Incline press = closest movement pattern (specificity).
Flat bench: ↑ max strength, less specific. Med ball pass: light/ballistic.
Section 01 — Program Design · 3 of 10

Rep Range Zone

A program prescribes 3–6RM loads for 4–6 reps. Which training goal does this rep range target?
  • APower
  • BStrength
  • CHypertrophy

Answer: B — Strength

Why
6RM ≈ 85% 1RM, 3RM ≈ 93% 1RM → heavy load + low reps = strength.
Hypertrophy: more reps (≈8+) at lower % 1RM.
Power: explosive reps at moderate/light load.

Key idea
Likely direction: isometric hold / plank → trunk stability without repeated spinal flexion.
Avoid loaded spinal flexion/rotation.
Section 01 — Program Design · 5 of 10

Sled Progression

An athlete has been pulling a 50 kg sled. How should training progress in week 4?
  • AIncrease sled weight to 60 kg
  • BAdd assisted sprinting technique

Likely answer: B — Add assisted sprinting technique

Why
Heavier sled → ↓ sprint velocity; trains force more than speed.
Assisted sprinting → ↑ stride velocity (overspeed) → true speed progression.
More load alone = same stimulus, just harder.
Section 01 — Program Design · 6 of 10

Endurance Progression

A runner's plan: Week 1 = 30-min long run. Week 2 = 35-min long run. Week 3 = 35-min tempo run. What is the best Week 4?
  • A40-min tempo run
  • B45-min interval session

Answer: B — 45-min interval session

Why
Tempo block ≈ 20–30 min at lactate threshold → stretching it to 40 min = more of the same.
Intervals: 3–5 min near VO2max, work:rest 1:1.
Adds a new stimulus instead of repeating tempo.
Section 01 — Program Design · 7 of 10

Tennis Player Power Drop

A tennis player's vertical jump and squat results have dropped while he runs long distances (~5 km). Which program adjustment is best?
  • AReduce running AND reduce resistance training to 2 days/week
  • BEliminate resistance training AND reduce running to 2 days/week
  • CEliminate running AND reduce resistance training to 2 days/week

Likely answer: A — Reduce running AND reduce resistance training to 2 days/week

Why
Heavy aerobic volume + strength training → interference → ↓ power.
Best fix: lower the load of both → ↓ running + resistance at 2 days/wk.
Dropping a whole mode is too drastic: strength still needed, some aerobic base still useful.
Section 01 — Program Design · 8 of 10

Patellofemoral Pain

An athlete has patellar (patellofemoral) pain. What is the best modification?
  • AModify 90° squat to a 45° squat
  • BUse a knee extension machine

Answer: A — Modify 90° squat to a 45° squat

Why
Deep knee flexion under load ↑ patellofemoral compression.
Limit squat to ≈45° (partial range) → ↓ joint stress.
Knee extension machine = open chain; stress ↑ near full extension.
Section 01 — Program Design · 9 of 10

Agility: Key Component

Which component matters most in agility?
  • AReaction
  • BEccentric strength
  • CConcentric strength

Answer: A — Reaction

Why
Agility = react to a stimulus, then change direction.
Reaction comes first → separates agility from planned change of direction.
Eccentric/concentric strength execute the move; they don't start it.
Section 01 — Program Design · 10 of 10

Early Support Phase

In the early support phase of running, which muscles drive propulsion?
  • AHamstrings & Glutes
  • BCore & Hip flexors

Answer: A — Hamstrings & Glutes

Why
Early support = foot just landed; hip extension continues concentrically.
Hamstrings + glutes extend the hip → push body forward.
Hip flexors work later: bring the leg through.

Section 02 — Exercise Technique · 1 of 5

Bike Fit

A cyclist cannot hold the target pace. Which bike adjustment is needed?
  • AMove seat forward
  • BMove seat back
  • CRaise handlebars
Answer to be confirmed. Stem details were not recalled.
Key idea
Seat fore/aft changes hip + knee angles → shifts load between quads and hamstrings/glutes.
Handlebar height changes trunk angle + hip flexion.
Pick the adjustment that fixes the fault shown in the question.
Section 02 — Exercise Technique · 2 of 5

Single-Leg Knee Shake

In a single-leg exercise video, the athlete's knee shakes visibly. What should be improved?
  • AImprove balance
  • BImprove glute medius

Likely answer: B — Improve glute medius

Why
Knee shake in single-leg stance = poor frontal-plane hip control.
Glute medius steadies pelvis + femur → knee tracks straight.
Balance drills help, but weak hip abductors are the root cause.
Section 02 — Exercise Technique · 3 of 5

Treadmill Start

What is the correct way to start a treadmill session?
  • AStraddle the belt (stand on side rails, step on once moving)
  • BPlace both feet on the belt

Answer: A — Straddle the belt (stand on side rails, step on once moving)

Why
Stand on the side rails, start the belt at low speed, then step on.
Both feet on a belt that starts → ↑ risk of falling.
Section 02 — Exercise Technique · 4 of 5

Atlas Stone Forward Drift

During an atlas stone/ball deadlift, the athlete drifts forward and drops the ball. What is the correction?
  • APut weight on heels
  • BPerform the Valsalva maneuver

Answer: A — Put weight on heels

Why
Forward drift = weight shifting onto the toes.
Weight on heels → re-centers body mass over the base.
Valsalva (bracing) belongs on every lift — it doesn't fix drift.
Section 02 — Exercise Technique · 5 of 5

Step Exercise Foot Placement

In a step exercise (step height 4–8 inch), which technique is correct?
  • APlace full heel on the pedal / step
  • BTake "deep steps"

Likely answer: A — Place full heel on the pedal / step

Why
Plant the full foot, heel included, on the step.
Heel contact → rolls heel-to-toe → full ankle/knee/hip extension before the next step.
Stay within the set 4–8 in step height.
Section 03

Program
Implementation

Edgren Side-Step Test — Protocol
  1. Setup 4 m line, markers every 1 m. Flat, safe surface.
  2. Start Feet together at one end, facing forward.
  3. Test Side-step over the line and back, no crossing, 15 s. Count successful steps.
  4. Trials 3 trials, ~30 s rest between. Record the best score.
Section 03 — Program Implementation · 1 of 4

Change-of-Direction Test

Which change-of-direction test suits a volleyball or basketball player?
  • AHexagon Test (6-direction jump)
  • BEdgren Side-Step Test (cones, lateral stepping)
  • CT-test
Answer to be confirmed. The stem was only partly recalled.
Key idea
Match the test to the sport movement.
Hexagon = double-leg hops in 6 directions, 3 laps. Side-step = lateral shuffles between cones. T-test = forward / lateral / backpedal pattern.
Section 03 — Program Implementation · 2 of 4

Power Test Battery

Which test battery best assesses a tennis player's power? Each battery has a vertical jump, standing broad jump and agility test; only the last test differs.
  • ABattery ending in 1RM Squat
  • BBattery ending in Power Clean

Likely answer: B — Battery ending in Power Clean

Why
Power = force × speed → jumps + power clean test power.
1RM squat tests maximal strength, not power.
Choose tests that match the quality being assessed.

Section 03 — Program Implementation · 4 of 4

Z-Score

Which statement correctly describes a z-score?
  • Options to be added
Answer to be confirmed. Options to be added.
Key idea
z = (score − group mean) ÷ standard deviation.
Shows how many SDs a score sits above/below the mean.
e.g. 40-yd dash 4.6 s, mean 5.00, SD 0.33 → z ≈ −1.2 (faster than average).

Organization

Section 04 — Organization & Administration · 1 of 11

Facility Design Priority

When designing a facility, what should be considered first?
  • AEfficient use of venue
  • BAthlete safety
  • CCompetition-based venue view

Answer: B — Athlete safety

Why
Safety first: equipment and safety spacing are never compromised to save space.
Clear exits + traffic flow + supervisor sightlines.
Efficiency and competition needs come after.
Section 04 — Organization & Administration · 2 of 11

New Coach: First Duty

A newly joined assistant strength and conditioning coach starts work. What should be their first duty?
  • AReview Policies & Procedures
  • BDevelop Training Program

Answer: A — Review Policies & Procedures

Why
Know the rules before acting.
Policies/procedures cover safety, emergency steps, legal limits.
Programming comes after.
Section 04 — Organization & Administration · 3 of 11

Heat Stroke

An athlete shows signs of heat stroke. What is the right response?
  • AElevate legs
  • BCall for medical help

Answer: B — Call for medical help

Why
Heat stroke = life-threatening emergency.
Activate emergency medical help + start rapid cooling at once.
Elevating the legs suits faintness, not heat stroke.
Section 04 — Organization & Administration · 4 of 11

Facility Rules Orientation

After reviewing the facility rules with athletes, how should you document that they understood them?
  • ASign & date acknowledgment
  • BStore the document (e.g., in a locker)
  • C"Retention exam"-style option

Answer: A — Sign & date acknowledgment

Why
Signed + dated copy = proof the athlete read and agreed to the rules.
Cuts the "I didn't know" excuse if rules are broken.
Section 04 — Organization & Administration · 5 of 11

Director's Top Duty

Which responsibility is most important for a strength and conditioning director?
  • AEffectively supervise
  • BMake policies and rules

Answer: B — Make policies and rules

Why
Written policies set the standard for staff, athletes and facility.
Supervision follows the policies.
Section 04 — Organization & Administration · 6 of 11

Equipment Planning

Which statement is correct when planning facility equipment?
  • AYoung athletes → free weights
  • BOlder adults → machines
  • CEquipment available for every body size

Likely answer: B — Older adults → machines

Why
Equipment mix follows the user group.
Mostly older users → more machines, fewer free weights.
Section 04 — Organization & Administration · 7 of 11

Injured Athlete: Knee Flexion

An injured athlete cannot reach the prescribed knee flexion without pain. What should you do?
  • ALet them continue as prescribed
  • BConsult Sports Medicine team

Answer: B — Consult Sports Medicine team

Why
Pain on movement = medical issue.
Coach doesn't diagnose or train through it → refer to the sports medicine team.
Section 04 — Organization & Administration · 8 of 11

Athlete Welfare

A female athlete shows weight loss and possible eating-disorder signs after a recent breakup. What should the coach do?
  • AFollow (school) follow-up procedure
  • BConfront the athlete
  • CTalk to parents

Answer: A — Follow (school) follow-up procedure

Why
Follow the institution's referral procedure.
Coach doesn't diagnose, confront, or inform parents alone.
Refer → qualified professionals.
Section 04 — Organization & Administration · 9 of 11

Wheelchair Access

How should a facility accommodate wheelchair users?
  • AIncrease spacing between equipment
  • BProvide a separate area

Answer: A — Increase spacing between equipment

Why
Wider walkways + equipment spacing → same space, same access for all.
Separate area = exclusion.
Section 04 — Organization & Administration · 10 of 11

Rehab Scheduling

Which scheduling priority applies to rehab clients in the facility?
  • ARehab clients scheduled in slower / off-peak hours
  • More options to be added
Answer to be confirmed. Only one option was recalled.
Key idea
Likely direction: rehab sessions go in slower hours.
Frees peak times for team sessions + gives rehab clients space and attention.
Section 04 — Organization & Administration · 11 of 11

Equipment Selection

When selecting machine equipment, which feature is most important?
  • ACam shape
  • BGradation of weight increments
  • CAdjustability of components

Answer: C — Adjustability of components

Why
Adjustable seat height / range / speed → fits different body sizes.
Works for everyone in the facility.
Cam shape + weight steps are secondary.
